scope.epoll: Four processes, 2000 iterations each on one queue/pipe pair: ADD, MOD with one-shot/data, write/check byte via wait/read, DEL.
scope.inotify: Four processes, 2000 add-watch/remove-watch/consume-IN_IGNORED cycles each on a private temporary directory.
scope.tcp: Unchanged complete TCP fixture, 256 sessions per process.
scope.timing: Median of three unprofiled counterbalanced repetitions and separate profiling samples. Queue/pipe/directory creation and teardown excluded from child loop but included in wall time.
scope.native_reference: Identical static ARM64 Linux ELF in both Trames versions and native Linux. Same C source on native macOS uses kqueue equivalents. Existing Linux reference: six vCPUs, 8 GiB configured; stopped before Mac timing and after targeted CI.
limitations: macOS equivalents use kqueue READ/EV_DISPATCH or VNODE add/delete/drain; notification payloads and syscall sequences differ from Linux.
Native TCP/task-signal/nested or unsupported epoll interests retain owner authority; epoll creation is a single-caller owner service, while factory and close/dup ownership remain owner-side.
Socket creation/full teardown/connect/accept, task/signal registry and scoped VM/device registration work remains.
No new resource-service thread, polling bus, guest quota/race errno or guest-memory barriers. Existing cursor/watch and source/publication synchronization remain object-local.
Cohort/owner counts include startup/teardown; summed caller waits are not CPU utilization. These fixtures do not establish whole-application or Firefox speedups.
Native Linux and macOS have different kernels and CPU allocation.
Final post-timing edits are architecture text and standalone ownership comments; production Rust code text is unchanged and passing validation was reused.
Physical iPad checks remain skipped per owner; its static cross-build passed.
